Name: Young Scholars Summer STEMM Research Program
Subject: Science
Description: The Young Scholars Summer STEMM Research Program is a free 6-week in-person summer 2026 program running from May 29 to August 1, with a priority application deadline of March 31, 2026, and requiring a full-time commitment with a pre-program orientation, placing approximately 30-40 selected rising 10th–12th graders (about 15-18 years old) from Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Missouri, Iowa, and Wisconsin onto research teams at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in Urbana-Champaign, Illinois, operating primarily as a commuter program where students arrange their own lodging and transportation. The program prioritizes underrepresented or under-resourced students with strong academic interest in STEMM and requires transcripts, recommendations, and essays for competitive selection based on motivation, grades, and fit for intensive research. Participants work in fields such as cancer immunology, neuroscience, AI/machine learning, physics, or bioengineering, committing 30–35 hours per week to lab work and related research activities, developing authentic research skills and culminating in a poster presentation and symposium showcasing their projects.

Name: Scientific Enrichment Month (SEM)
Subject: Science
Description: The Scientific Enrichment Month program at the Herbert Irving Comprehensive Cancer Center at Columbia University is a free enrichment program where student can gain knowledge on cancer science and biomedical research. This program has a registration instead of an application, so while the due date is in June 19, 2026, the capacity may be met before then. Participants of this program can learn from virtual lectures, workshops, and discussions with real scientists and medical professionals. This program is perfect for those who want an introduction to research careers, scientific inquiry, and health sciences. In addition, this program provides high school students with professional development and mentorship opportunities. If interested in biology, medicine, or research careers to gain early exposure to the field, make sure to check out this great opportunity.

Name: 2026 Double Discovery Center Summer Academy
Subject: Research
Description: The Double Discovery Center Summer Academy is a free enrichment program hosted by Columbia University that is available to all low-income or first-generation college-bound high school students in grades 9-10. Students are given the chance to attend four weeks of classes on Columbia's campus, taking real courses in research, writing, and critical thinking while preparing for the college application process. Additionally, this program provides workshops in financial aid, mentorship, college advising, and campus life experiences. For those looking for a structured summer experience that shows commitment to high education, this program focusing heavily on college readiness is perfect.

Name: DCTV Youth Media Summer Intensive
Subject: Film
Description: The DCTV Youth Media Summer Intensive is a free four-week filmmaking and media creation program from July 6 to July 31 that is open to youth ages 14-21 in NYC. This program is perfect for anyone interested in camera work, and during, storytelling, and media production. This course helps participants express their creativity through pitching ideas and producing film or projects. Additionally this is a great free opportunity to learn more about editing softwares and equipment operation. Applications are due by Sunday, May 3, 2026 (end of day deadline typical).

Name: Ocean Guardian Youth Ambassador Program
Subject: Science
Description: Interested in marine life and the conservation of our oceans? If yes, then the Ocean Guardian Youth Ambassador program is for you! This virtual program, made for anyone age 13-18, discusses every aspect of ocean conservation. Not only does the Ambassador program consist of an abundance of opportunities to collaborate with marine scientists and experts in the field, but it will also allow for you to gain hands-on experience in leadership. Part of the Ambassadors program includes the monthly webinars, where you have the chance to learn about threats to the ocean, ocean conservation efforts, further programs and careers in regards to marine science, alongside other opportunities to emphasize leadership. The program runs from January to December, and applications for the 2026-2027 year will open on November 13th and close on January 3rd.

Name: Columbia Science Honors Program
Subject: Science
Description: The Columbia Unversity Science Honors Program is an extremely competitive, prestigious opportunity to receive in-person instruction and access to college-level courses at Columbia University whilst being in high school. Courses in astrophysics, organic chemistry, material science, and bioengineering are typically offered. The program takes place on Saturday mornings during the entire academic year. Students will commute to Columbia University’s Morningside campus to attend a class. Students in tenth, eleventh, and twelfth grade are all welcome to apply. The application is currently open, and will close on April 15th. The application has a $50 fee, and requires a completed online application with a letter of recommendation from either a math or science teacher, or a guidance counselor or a principal, alongside a high school transcript. Part of the application also involves a two-hour long assessment in mathematics and science. For any inquiries regarding Columbia University SHP, one may contact them at shp@columbia.edu. Lastly, the program cost is $700 per year, with $350 being paid at the start of each semester.

Name: Beauty + Health: Youth Graphic Medicine Challenge
Subject: Art
Description: The Youth Graphic Medicine Challenge, hosted by the National Institute of Health, is a great opportunity for teens aged 13-17 to show off artistic creativity alongside creating awareness. This challenge involves the creation of original comics about ways to reduce health risks from beauty products and behaviors. Entries will provide insights into the perspective of young people in regards to experiences involving beauty products or behaviors, and such may assist in informing future research to develop preventions to beauty risks. The competition’s submission period ends on April 2nd. There is $17,000 in winnings, with first, second, and third places winning $3,500, $2,500, and $1,500 respectively. There is no fee for entry, but the entry form does require a brief title and caption to be given in regards to the comic being submitted.
